summary: Yadkin County, NC: a fire tower built in 1959 beside a 1954 survey mark; a 1992 note places the mark by the tower, and no source describes it today.

facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey set the survey mark on the highest point about 3 miles southeast of Boonville
Fire tower constructed 12 feet east of the survey mark in September 1959, per a 1960 North Carolina Division of Forestry recovery note
North Carolina Geodetic Survey recovery note places the mark on the west side of the fire tower
North Carolina Geodetic Survey recovery: mark in good condition near a chain-link fence; the note does not describe the tower

notes_for_editor: Two sources only. The 1959 build date and the 1992 presence of the tower come from NC agency recovery notes inside the NGS datasheet. No source gives height, design, staffing, access or condition of the tower after 1992. Two social posts in the cache mention the tower (a Facebook group post saying 100 ft, built 1959, standing, cabin locked; and an NC Fire Towers Instagram caption calling it a 100 ft Aermotor tower, photo dated January 2021). Neither was cited: the Facebook text sits in script blocks that fetch_text drops, so its quote cannot be checked, and the Instagram post URL was not in the cache. A human check of the tower's current state, or an NC Division of Forest Resources contact, would settle it. WebSearch budget was used up in this run. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the story's present-tense 'is a fire tower' was changed to past tense, since no source shows the tower after 1992; the advice to ask the NC Division of Forest Resources and not to climb any tower was removed because the Forest Lookouts index does not say it.
